skill.name: remotion-to-hyperframes
skill.description: Translate existing Remotion video compositions into HyperFrames HTML. The skill maps supported APIs, flags unsupported React patterns, and guides visual validation.
skill.summary: Convert Remotion compositions to HyperFrames with linting, API mapping, and render validation.
skill.author: heygen-com

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, fixture code, quoted validation commands, and local harness scripts. No prompt injection, credential harvesting, or hidden exfiltration intent was found. The main residual risk is the opt-in eval harness, which can install npm dependencies and run local render/media tools.

remediation.issue: Eval harness performs npm install for fixtures.
remediation.suggestion: Add lockfiles or use npm ci with --ignore-scripts, and document that validation may access the npm registry.

remediation.issue: Fixture HTML loads third-party CDN scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Pin resources with SRI or vendor local copies for offline, reproducible validation.

remediation.issue: Render and diff helpers invoke ffmpeg, ffprobe, node, and npx.
remediation.suggestion: Keep these scripts opt-in, validate input paths, and document required local toolchain permissions.

semantic_findings.description: The corpus runner invokes npm install inside fixture projects before rendering baselines. This is documented and intended, but it can reach the npm registry and run dependency lifecycle scripts unless constrained.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The cited line directly invokes npm install when fixture node_modules is missing. The risk is supply-chain exposure during opt-in validation, not hidden malicious intent.

content.value_statement: Teams moving video work from Remotion need a repeatable translation path. This skill maps Remotion APIs to HyperFrames HTML, flags blockers, and validates visual parity.
actual_capabilities: Lint Remotion source for blockers such as React state, async metadata, and unsupported UI libraries.
Map Remotion Composition, Sequence, timing, media, fonts, transitions, and Lottie APIs to HyperFrames equivalents.
Generate an HTML composition structure with data attributes, CSS, and a paused GSAP timeline.
Recommend runtime interop when source patterns cannot translate safely.
Validate translations with Remotion and HyperFrames renders using SSIM diff scripts.
Document dropped or approximated features in TRANSLATION_NOTES.md.
limitations: It only applies when a user explicitly asks to migrate existing Remotion source.
It refuses deterministic translation for stateful React logic and side-effect driven animation.
It may approximate unsupported media behavior, custom transitions, or third-party components.
End-to-end validation requires local Node, npm, Remotion, HyperFrames CLI, ffmpeg, and ffprobe.

use_cases.title: Port Product Video Templates
use_cases.description: Translate existing Remotion templates into HyperFrames while preserving timing, props, and visual checks.

use_cases.title: Audit Migration Feasibility
use_cases.description: Run the lint rules to find blockers before committing to a rewrite.

use_cases.title: Validate Translation Quality
use_cases.description: Compare source and translated renders with SSIM metrics and frame strips.

prompt_templates.title: Check If My Project Can Translate
prompt_templates.prompt: Use remotion-to-hyperframes to lint my Remotion source at ./src and summarize blockers, warnings, and next steps.

prompt_templates.title: Translate A Simple Composition
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this Remotion composition to HyperFrames HTML. Use the API map, keep props as data attributes, and write translation notes.

prompt_templates.title: Handle Unsupported Patterns
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Remotion project for state, effects, async metadata, and Lambda usage. Recommend translation or runtime interop with reasons.

prompt_templates.title: Validate And Debug A Migration
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the Remotion and HyperFrames renders, compare SSIM, inspect failing frames, and list precise fixes for timing or media mismatches.

output_examples.input: A title-card Remotion component with a fade-in and static props.
output_examples.output: A HyperFrames HTML composition with one stage, one scene, matching duration, and a GSAP fade timeline.

output_examples.input: A Remotion project that uses useState and a side-effect driven animation.
output_examples.output: A refusal to translate directly, with a runtime interop recommendation and the specific blocker rules.

output_examples.input: A migrated multi-scene video with audio and an image asset.
output_examples.output: A validation summary with SSIM pass or fail status, key mismatched frames, and notes for asset or timing fixes.

best_practices: Run the lint step before generating HTML so blockers are caught early.
Load only the reference files needed for APIs used by the source project.
Render both outputs with matching pixel format before comparing SSIM.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for new HyperFrames work that is not a source migration.
Do not translate React state machines into static timelines.
Do not skip TRANSLATION_NOTES.md when features are dropped or approximated.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it only when you explicitly need to migrate existing Remotion source into HyperFrames.

faq.question: Does it support every Remotion API?
faq.answer: No. It maps common APIs and refuses patterns that cannot preserve deterministic frame behavior.

faq.question: What happens when the source uses React state?
faq.answer: The lint step reports a blocker and recommends the runtime interop approach instead of direct translation.

faq.question: Can it validate visual accuracy?
faq.answer: Yes. The included workflow compares Remotion and HyperFrames renders with SSIM metrics.

faq.question: Does validation require external tools?
faq.answer: Yes. Full validation needs Node, npm, Remotion, the HyperFrames CLI, ffmpeg, and ffprobe.

faq.question: Will it document lossy changes?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow calls for TRANSLATION_NOTES.md when features are dropped or approximated.
